subject: Efficient sampling from a block diagonal (known) covariance matrix

messages.author: 145936f19be1abc9
messages.subject: Efficient sampling from a block diagonal (known) covariance matrix
parts:
Hello guys,

my issue is the following. I have several 'populations' of individuals of variable size but with known covariance matrices.
Suppose individuals from different populations are independent and it would be thus more efficient to sample conditional on the
populations instead of sampling from a huge block diagonal matrix with lots of zeros. How can I achieve this in RStan?

As an R user, two possibilities come to my mind:
1) Using a list of matrices and sampling from one after the other
2) Subsetting a huge block diagonal matrix appropriately when sampling

I appreciate your help,
Dominik

messages.subject: Re: Efficient sampling from a block diagonal (known) covariance matrix
parts:
On Thursday, July 24, 2014 6:33:29 AM UTC-4, dominom...@googlemail.com wrote:
my issue is the following. I have several 'populations' of individuals of variable size but with known covariance matrices.
Suppose individuals from different populations are independent and it would be thus more efficient to sample conditional on the
populations instead of sampling from a huge block diagonal matrix with lots of zeros. How can I achieve this in RStan?

As an R user, two possibilities come to my mind:
1) Using a list of matrices and sampling from one after the other
2) Subsetting a huge block diagonal matrix appropriately when sampling

Subsetting is more tedious in Stan than it is in R, so I would go with option 1). You need to declare an array of covariance matrices in the data block like

data {
  int<lower=1> n_populations;
  int<lower=2> n_variables;
  cov_matrix[n_variables] Sigma[n_populations];
}
...

And then include a list of those covariance matrices as an element of the data list when you call stan() from R.

Ben
